v: The word of the LORD[^1] that came to Hosea[^2] son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.[^3]
דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֗ה אֶל־הוֹשֵׁ֙עַ֙ בֶּן־בְּאֵרִ֔י בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֥ה יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖ה מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבִימֵ֛י יָרָבְעָ֥ם בֶּן־יוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife given to prostitution, and children of prostitution,[^4] for the land is committing flagrant prostitution by turning away from the LORD."
תְּחִלַּ֥ת דִּבֶּר־יְהוָ֖ה בְּהוֹשֵׁ֑עַ פ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לֵ֣ךְ קַח־לְךָ֞ אֵ֤שֶׁת זְנוּנִים֙ וְיַלְדֵ֣י זְנוּנִ֔ים כִּֽי־זָנֹ֤ה תִזְנֶה֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵֽאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
So he went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיִּקַּ֔ח אֶת־גֹּ֖מֶר בַּת־דִּבְלָ֑יִם וַתַּ֥הַר וַתֵּֽלֶד־ל֖וֹ בֵּֽן׃
The LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel,[^5] for in a little while I will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed of Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו קְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יִזְרְעֶ֑אל כִּי־ע֣וֹד מְעַ֗ט וּפָ֨קַדְתִּ֜י אֶת־דְּמֵ֤י יִזְרְעֶאל֙ עַל־בֵּ֣ית יֵה֔וּא וְהִ֨שְׁבַּתִּ֔י מַמְלְכ֖וּת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
On that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."
וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְשָֽׁבַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־קֶ֣שֶׁת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּעֵ֖מֶק יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃
She conceived again and bore a daughter. The LORD said to him,[^6] "Name her Lo-ruhamah,[^7] for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should forgive them at all.[^8]
וַתַּ֤הַר עוֹד֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בַּ֔ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ קְרָ֥א שְׁמָ֖הּ לֹ֣א רֻחָ֑מָה כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אוֹסִ֜יף ע֗וֹד אֲרַחֵם֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּֽי־נָשֹׂ֥א אֶשָּׂ֖א לָהֶֽם׃
But I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the LORD their God. I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen."
וְאֶת־בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙ אֲרַחֵ֔ם וְהֽוֹשַׁעְתִּ֖ים בַּיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וְלֹ֣א אֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֗ם בְּקֶ֤שֶׁת וּבְחֶ֙רֶב֙ וּבְמִלְחָמָ֔ה בְּסוּסִ֖ים וּבְפָרָשִֽׁים׃
After she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.
וַתִּגְמֹ֖ל אֶת־לֹ֣א רֻחָ֑מָה וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּֽן׃
The LORD said, "Name him Lo-ammi,[^9] for you are not my people, and I will not be yours."[^10]
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר קְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ לֹ֣א עַמִּ֑י כִּ֤י אַתֶּם֙ לֹ֣א עַמִּ֔י וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹֽא־אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *Hoshea*, "salvation" or "he has saved", the original name of Joshua (Numbers 13:16) and the name of the last king of Israel (2 Kings 17:1).
n.3: Jeroboam II reigned from about 786 to 746 BC. Hosea's work as a prophet ran from the last years of Jeroboam's reign until shortly before the fall of Samaria in 722 BC.
n.4: Literally "a wife of prostitutions and children of prostitutions". Hebrew *zenunim*, "prostitution, sexual unfaithfulness". It need not mean that she was a professional prostitute; it may mean that she was, or would become, unfaithful. Throughout the book the word pictures Israel's worship of other gods as a wife's unfaithfulness to her husband.
n.5: Jezreel means "God sows". It was the royal city and valley where Jehu seized the throne by killing the family of Ahab (2 Kings 9–10). The name returns as a promise in 2:2, 24–25 (1:11; 2:22–23 in most English Bibles).
n.6: Literally "He said to him". Also in verse 9.
n.7: Lo-ruhamah means "not shown compassion" or "not loved". The Hebrew verb *racham* is used of the tender love of a parent.
n.8: Or "but I will surely take them away". The Hebrew verb *nasa*, "lift up, carry", can mean "forgive" (bear away sin) or "take away".
n.10: Literally "and I, I will not be to you". Hebrew *lo-ehyeh*, "I will not be", probably echoes the name God gives himself in Exodus 3:14, *ehyeh*, "I am" or "I will be". Many translations, following the context and 2:25 (2:23 in most English Bibles), read "and I am not your God".

v: Yet the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted.[^1] And in the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God."[^2]
וְֽ֠הָיָה מִסְפַּ֤ר בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יִמַּ֖ד וְלֹ֣א יִסָּפֵ֑ר וְֽ֠הָיָה בִּמְק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יֵאָמֵ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לֹֽא־עַמִּ֣י אַתֶּ֔ם יֵאָמֵ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י אֵֽל־חָֽי׃
The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together. They will appoint for themselves one head, and they will go up from the land,[^3] for great will be the day of Jezreel.
וְ֠נִקְבְּצוּ בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֤ה וּבְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו וְשָׂמ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם רֹ֥אשׁ אֶחָ֖ד וְעָל֣וּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֥י גָד֖וֹל י֥וֹם יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃
Say to your brothers, "Ammi," and to your sisters, "Ruhamah."[^4]
אִמְר֥וּ לַאֲחֵיכֶ֖ם עַמִּ֑י וְלַאֲחֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם רֻחָֽמָה׃
Bring charges against your mother, bring charges, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove her prostitution from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,
רִ֤יבוּ בְאִמְּכֶם֙ רִ֔יבוּ כִּֽי־הִיא֙ לֹ֣א אִשְׁתִּ֔י וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֣א אִישָׁ֑הּ וְתָסֵ֤ר זְנוּנֶ֙יהָ֙ מִפָּנֶ֔יה וְנַאֲפוּפֶ֖יהָ מִבֵּ֥ין שָׁדֶֽיהָ׃
or I will strip her naked and expose her as on the day she was born. I will make her like a wilderness, turn her into a parched land, and kill her with thirst.
פֶּן־אַפְשִׁיטֶ֣נָּה עֲרֻמָּ֔ה וְהִ֨צַּגְתִּ֔יהָ כְּי֖וֹם הִוָּֽלְדָ֑הּ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣יהָ כַמִּדְבָּ֗ר וְשַׁתִּ֙הָ֙ כְּאֶ֣רֶץ צִיָּ֔ה וַהֲמִתִּ֖יהָ בַּצָּמָֽא׃
I will have no compassion on her children, because they are children of prostitution.
וְאֶת־בָּנֶ֖יהָ לֹ֣א אֲרַחֵ֑ם כִּֽי־בְנֵ֥י זְנוּנִ֖ים הֵֽמָּה׃

For their mother has prostituted herself; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
כִּ֤י זָֽנְתָה֙ אִמָּ֔ם הֹבִ֖ישָׁה הֽוֹרָתָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמְרָ֗ה אֵלְכָ֞ה אַחֲרֵ֤י מְאַהֲבַי֙ נֹתְנֵ֤י לַחְמִי֙ וּמֵימַ֔י צַמְרִ֣י וּפִשְׁתִּ֔י שַׁמְנִ֖י וְשִׁקּוּיָֽי׃
Therefore I am going to hedge up your way with thorns,[^5] and I will build a wall against her, so that she cannot find her paths.
לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִי־שָׂ֥ךְ אֶת־דַּרְכֵּ֖ךְ בַּסִּירִ֑ים וְגָֽדַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־גְּדֵרָ֔הּ וּנְתִיבוֹתֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א תִמְצָֽא׃
She will pursue her lovers but not overtake them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now."
וְרִדְּפָ֤ה אֶת־מְאַהֲבֶ֙יהָ֙ וְלֹֽא־תַשִּׂ֣יג אֹתָ֔ם וּבִקְשָׁ֖תַם וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָ֑א וְאָמְרָ֗ה אֵלְכָ֤ה וְאָשׁ֙וּבָה֙ אֶל־אִישִׁ֣י הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לִ֛י אָ֖ז מֵעָֽתָּה׃
She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, and who lavished on her the silver and gold that they used for Baal.[^6]
וְהִיא֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְעָ֔ה כִּ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔הּ הַדָּגָ֖ן וְהַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֑ר וְכֶ֨סֶף הִרְבֵּ֥יתִי לָ֛הּ וְזָהָ֖ב עָשׂ֥וּ לַבָּֽעַל׃
Therefore I will take back my grain in its time and my new wine in its season, and I will snatch away my wool and my flax, which were to cover her nakedness.
לָכֵ֣ן אָשׁ֔וּב וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י דְגָנִי֙ בְּעִתּ֔וֹ וְתִירוֹשִׁ֖י בְּמֽוֹעֲד֑וֹ וְהִצַּלְתִּי֙ צַמְרִ֣י וּפִשְׁתִּ֔י לְכַסּ֖וֹת אֶת־עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃
Now I will uncover her shame[^7] before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hand.
וְעַתָּ֛ה אֲגַלֶּ֥ה אֶת־נַבְלֻתָ֖הּ לְעֵינֵ֣י מְאַהֲבֶ֑יהָ וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹֽא־יַצִּילֶ֥נָּה מִיָּדִֽי׃
I will put an end to all her celebrations: her festivals, her new moons, her Sabbaths and all her appointed feasts.
וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ כָּל־מְשׂוֹשָׂ֔הּ חַגָּ֖הּ חָדְשָׁ֣הּ וְשַׁבַּתָּ֑הּ וְכֹ֖ל מוֹעֲדָֽהּ׃
I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she said, "These are my wages,[^8] which my lovers gave me." I will turn them into a thicket, and the wild animals will devour them.
וַהֲשִׁמֹּתִ֗י גַּפְנָהּ֙ וּתְאֵ֣נָתָ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמְרָ֗ה אֶתְנָ֥ה הֵ֙מָּה֙ לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָֽתְנוּ־לִ֖י מְאַֽהֲבָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֣ים לְיַ֔עַר וַאֲכָלָ֖תַם חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

I will punish her for the feast days of the Baals,[^9] when she burned incense[^10] to them and decked herself with her nose ring and her jewelry, and went after her lovers, but me she forgot, declares the LORD.[^11]
וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י עָלֶ֗יהָ אֶת־יְמֵ֤י הַבְּעָלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּקְטִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם וַתַּ֤עַד נִזְמָהּ֙ וְחֶלְיָתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֣י מְאַהֲבֶ֑יהָ וְאֹתִ֥י שָׁכְחָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ פ
Therefore I am going to win her back.[^12] I will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her.[^13]
לָכֵ֗ן הִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מְפַתֶּ֔יהָ וְהֹֽלַכְתִּ֖יהָ הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְדִבַּרְתִּ֖י עַל[c] לִבָּֽהּ׃

There I will give her back her vineyards, and make the Valley of Achor[^14] a door of hope. There she will respond[^15] as in the days of her youth, as on the day she came up out of the land of Egypt.
וְנָתַ֨תִּי לָ֤הּ אֶת־כְּרָמֶ֙יהָ֙ מִשָּׁ֔ם וְאֶת־עֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְפֶ֣תַח תִּקְוָ֑ה וְעָ֤נְתָה שָּׁ֙מָּה֙ כִּימֵ֣י נְעוּרֶ֔יהָ וִּכְי֖וֹם עֲלֹתָ֥הּ מֵאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרָֽיִם׃ ס
On that day, declares the LORD, you will call me "My husband," and you will no longer call me "My Baal."[^16]
וְהָיָ֤ה בַיּוֹם־הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה תִּקְרְאִ֖י אִישִׁ֑י וְלֹֽא־תִקְרְאִי־לִ֥י ע֖וֹד בַּעְלִֽי׃
I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be remembered by name.
וַהֲסִרֹתִ֛י אֶת־שְׁמ֥וֹת הַבְּעָלִ֖ים מִפִּ֑יהָ וְלֹֽא־יִזָּכְר֥וּ ע֖וֹד בִּשְׁמָֽם׃

On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds of the sky and the creatures that creep on the ground. I will break bow and sword and battle and banish them from the land, and I will let them lie down in safety.

וְכָרַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֤ם בְּרִית֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא עִם־חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְעִם־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְרֶ֖מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה וְקֶ֨שֶׁת וְחֶ֤רֶב וּמִלְחָמָה֙ אֶשְׁבּ֣וֹר מִן־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִשְׁכַּבְתִּ֖ים לָבֶֽטַח׃
I will betroth you to myself forever. I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and justice, in faithful love[^17] and compassion.
וְאֵרַשְׂתִּ֥יךְ לִ֖י לְעוֹלָ֑ם וְאֵרַשְׂתִּ֥יךְ לִי֙ בְּצֶ֣דֶק וּבְמִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּבְחֶ֖סֶד וּֽבְרַחֲמִֽים׃
I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
וְאֵרַשְׂתִּ֥יךְ לִ֖י בֶּאֱמוּנָ֑ה וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃ ס
On that day I will answer, declares the LORD. I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא אֶֽעֱנֶה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה אֶעֱנֶ֖ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְהֵ֖ם יַעֲנ֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The earth will answer the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, and they will answer Jezreel.[^18]
וְהָאָ֣רֶץ תַּעֲנֶ֔ה אֶת־הַדָּגָ֖ן וְאֶת־הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְאֶת־הַיִּצְהָ֑ר וְהֵ֖ם יַעֲנ֥וּ אֶֽת־יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃
I will sow her for myself in the land. I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, and I will say to Lo-ammi, "You are my people," and he will say, "My God."[^19]
וּזְרַעְתִּ֤יהָ לִּי֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־לֹ֣א רֻחָ֑מָה וְאָמַרְתִּ֤י לְלֹֽא־עַמִּי֙ עַמִּי־אַ֔תָּה וְה֖וּא יֹאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽי׃ פ

n.1: Verses 1–2 are 1:10–11 in most English Bibles, and verses 3–25 are 2:1–23. Compare the promise to Abraham (Genesis 22:17; 32:13, 32:12 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Or "and they will spring up from the land", like a crop (see "Jezreel", "God sows", in 1:4), or "and they will take possession of the land". The meaning is uncertain.
n.4: Ammi means "my people" and Ruhamah "shown compassion": the names of Hosea's children (1:6, 9) without "not".
n.6: Or "which they made into Baal", that is, into images of Baal. Baal, "lord, master", was the Canaanite storm god, believed to give rain and fertility to the land.
n.7: Hebrew *navlut*, a word found only here, perhaps "lewdness" or "genitals".
n.8: Hebrew *etnah*, the payment given to a prostitute.
n.9: The local forms of the god Baal worshiped at many shrines. Also in verse 19.
n.10: Or "burned offerings". The Hebrew verb *qatar* means to make something go up in smoke.
n.11: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Or "she will sing". Hebrew *anah*, "answer, respond", the same verb as in verses 23–24.
n.16: Hebrew *ishi*, "my husband" (literally "my man"), and *ba'ali*, "my master", also used for "my husband", and the name of the god Baal.
n.18: Jezreel, "God sows", here becomes a name of promise. Compare 1:4–5; 2:2.

v: The LORD[^1] said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man[^2] and is an adulteress, just as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love raisin cakes."[^3]

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י ע֚וֹד לֵ֣ךְ אֱ‍ֽהַב־אִשָּׁ֔ה אֲהֻ֥בַת רֵ֖עַ וּמְנָאָ֑פֶת כְּאַהֲבַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהֵ֗ם פֹּנִים֙ אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י אֲשִׁישֵׁ֥י עֲנָבִֽים׃
So I bought her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.[^4]
וָאֶכְּרֶ֣הָ לִּ֔י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר כָּ֑סֶף וְחֹ֥מֶר שְׂעֹרִ֖ים וְלֵ֥תֶךְ שְׂעֹרִֽים׃
Then I said to her, "You are to live with me for many days. You must not be a prostitute or belong to any man, and I too will be faithful to you."[^5]
וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֗יהָ יָמִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ תֵּ֣שְׁבִי לִ֔י לֹ֣א תִזְנִ֔י וְלֹ֥א תִֽהְיִ֖י לְאִ֑ישׁ וְגַם־אֲנִ֖י אֵלָֽיִךְ׃
For the Israelites will live for many days without king or official, without sacrifice or standing stone, without ephod or household gods.[^6]
כִּ֣י ׀ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים יֵֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ין מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ וְאֵ֣ין שָׂ֔ר וְאֵ֥ין זֶ֖בַח וְאֵ֣ין מַצֵּבָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין אֵפ֖וֹד וּתְרָפִֽים׃
Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king.[^7] They will come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness in the last days.[^8]
אַחַ֗ר יָשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבִקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת דָּוִ֣ד מַלְכָּ֑ם וּפָחֲד֧וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֛ה וְאֶל־טוּב֖וֹ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Or "who is loved by her husband". Hebrew *rea*, "friend, companion", which can also mean a lover or a husband (Jeremiah 3:20).
n.3: Cakes of pressed raisins were eaten at festivals (2 Samuel 6:19), here probably festivals of other gods.
n.4: A shekel was about ⅖ ounce (11.5 grams), so fifteen shekels were about 6 ounces (170 grams). A homer was probably about 6 bushels (220 liters). A *lethech* was perhaps half a homer.
n.5: Literally "and also I to you". Or "and I will not come to you either".
n.6: *Standing stones* (Hebrew *matsevot*) were set up as objects of worship. The *ephod* was a priestly garment, sometimes an object used to seek guidance from God (Judges 8:27; 17:5). *Household gods* is Hebrew *teraphim*, small images of gods kept in the home (Genesis 31:19).
n.7: That is, a king from the family of David.
n.8: Literally "at the end of the days".

v: Hear the word of the LORD,[^1] you Israelites, for the LORD has a case[^2] against those who live in the land. There is no faithfulness, no faithful love,[^3] no knowledge of God in the land.
שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י רִ֤יב לַֽיהוָה֙ עִם־יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֠י אֵין־אֱמֶ֧ת וְֽאֵין־חֶ֛סֶד וְאֵֽין־דַּ֥עַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
There is cursing, lying, murder, stealing and adultery.[^4] They break all bounds, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.[^5]
אָלֹ֣ה וְכַחֵ֔שׁ וְרָצֹ֥חַ וְגָנֹ֖ב וְנָאֹ֑ף פָּרָ֕צוּ וְדָמִ֥ים בְּדָמִ֖ים נָגָֽעוּ׃
Therefore the land mourns,[^6] and all who live in it waste away, along with the wild animals and the birds of the sky, and even the fish of the sea are swept away.
עַל־כֵּ֣ן ׀ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֗רֶץ וְאֻמְלַל֙ כָּל־יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בָּ֔הּ בְּחַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְגַם־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם יֵאָסֵֽפוּ׃
Yet let no one bring a charge, and let no one accuse, for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest.[^7]
אַ֥ךְ אִ֛ישׁ אַל־יָרֵ֖ב וְאַל־יוֹכַ֣ח אִ֑ישׁ וְעַמְּךָ֖ כִּמְרִיבֵ֥י כֹהֵֽן׃
You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night, and I will destroy your mother.[^8]
וְכָשַׁלְתָּ֣ הַיּ֔וֹם וְכָשַׁ֧ל גַּם־נָבִ֛יא עִמְּךָ֖ לָ֑יְלָה וְדָמִ֖יתִי אִמֶּֽךָ׃

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving as my priest. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
נִדְמ֥וּ עַמִּ֖י מִבְּלִ֣י הַדָּ֑עַת כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה הַדַּ֣עַת מָאַ֗סְתָּ וְאֶמְאָֽסְאךָ֙ מִכַּהֵ֣ן לִ֔י וַתִּשְׁכַּח֙ תּוֹרַ֣ת אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֶשְׁכַּ֥ח בָּנֶ֖יךָ גַּם־אָֽנִי׃
The more they increased, the more they sinned against me. I will change their glory into shame.[^9]
כְּרֻבָּ֖ם כֵּ֣ן חָֽטְאוּ־לִ֑י כְּבוֹדָ֖ם בְּקָל֥וֹן אָמִֽיר׃
They feed on the sin of my people,[^10] and they long for their iniquity.[^11]
חַטַּ֥את עַמִּ֖י יֹאכֵ֑לוּ וְאֶל־עֲוֺנָ֖ם יִשְׂא֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
It will be like people, like priest. I will punish them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.[^12]
וְהָיָ֥ה כָעָ֖ם כַּכֹּהֵ֑ן וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י עָלָיו֙ דְּרָכָ֔יו וּמַעֲלָלָ֖יו אָשִׁ֥יב לֽוֹ׃
They will eat but not be satisfied; they will prostitute themselves but not increase, for they have abandoned the LORD and stopped heeding him.[^13]
וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֔עוּ הִזְנ֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יִפְרֹ֑צוּ כִּֽי־אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה עָזְב֖וּ לִשְׁמֹֽר׃
Prostitution, wine and new wine take away understanding.[^14]
זְנ֛וּת וְיַ֥יִן וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ יִֽקַּֽח־לֵֽב׃
My people consult their piece of wood, and their staff gives them answers.[^15] For a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have prostituted themselves and left their God.[^16]
עַמִּי֙ בְּעֵצ֣וֹ יִשְׁאָ֔ל וּמַקְל֖וֹ יַגִּ֣יד ל֑וֹ כִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ זְנוּנִים֙ הִתְעָ֔ה וַיִּזְנ֖וּ מִתַּ֥חַת אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

They sacrifice on the tops of the mountains and burn incense on the hills, under oak, poplar and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. That is why your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
עַל־רָאשֵׁ֨י הֶהָרִ֜ים יְזַבֵּ֗חוּ וְעַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת֙ יְקַטֵּ֔רוּ תַּ֣חַת אַלּ֧וֹן וְלִבְנֶ֛ה וְאֵלָ֖ה כִּ֣י ט֣וֹב צִלָּ֑הּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן תִּזְנֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְכַלּוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם תְּנָאַֽפְנָה׃

I will not punish your daughters when they turn to prostitution, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for the men themselves go off with prostitutes and sacrifice with shrine prostitutes.[^17] A people without understanding will come to ruin.
לֹֽא־אֶפְק֨וֹד עַל־בְּנוֹתֵיכֶ֜ם כִּ֣י תִזְנֶ֗ינָה וְעַל־כַּלּֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ כִּ֣י תְנָאַ֔פְנָה כִּי־הֵם֙ עִם־הַזֹּנ֣וֹת יְפָרֵ֔דוּ וְעִם־הַקְּדֵשׁ֖וֹת יְזַבֵּ֑חוּ וְעָ֥ם לֹֽא־יָבִ֖ין יִלָּבֵֽט׃
Though you, Israel, play the prostitute, do not let Judah become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven,[^18] and do not swear, "As the LORD lives!"
אִם־זֹנֶ֤ה אַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַל־יֶאְשַׁ֖ם יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאַל־תָּבֹ֣אוּ הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל וְאַֽל־תַּעֲלוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אָ֔וֶן וְאַל־תִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ חַי־יְהוָֽה׃
For Israel is stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in a broad meadow?[^19]
כִּ֚י כְּפָרָ֣ה סֹֽרֵרָ֔ה סָרַ֖ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַתָּה֙ יִרְעֵ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה כְּכֶ֖בֶשׂ בַּמֶּרְחָֽב׃
Ephraim[^20] is joined to idols; leave him alone!
חֲב֧וּר עֲצַבִּ֛ים אֶפְרָ֖יִם הַֽנַּֽח־לֽוֹ׃
When their drinking is over, they give themselves to prostitution. Her rulers dearly love shame.[^21]
סָ֖ר סָבְאָ֑ם הַזְנֵ֣ה הִזְנ֔וּ אָהֲב֥וּ הֵב֛וּ קָל֖וֹן מָגִנֶּֽיהָ׃
A wind has wrapped her up in its wings,[^22] and they will be put to shame because of their sacrifices.[^23]
צָרַ֥ר ר֛וּחַ אוֹתָ֖הּ בִּכְנָפֶ֑יהָ וְיֵבֹ֖שׁוּ מִזִּבְחוֹתָֽם ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *riv*, a lawsuit or legal dispute.
n.4: The list recalls the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:7, 13–16; Deuteronomy 5:11, 17–20).
n.6: Or "dries up". The Hebrew verb can have either meaning.
n.7: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Some scholars read "for with you is my case, O priest", with small changes to the Hebrew.
n.8: Probably the nation (compare 2:4, 2:2 in most English Bibles), or the priest's own family. *Destroy* (Hebrew *damah*) is the same verb as "are destroyed" in verse 6.
n.9: According to an ancient Jewish scribal tradition (the "corrections of the scribes"), the original text read "They have exchanged my glory for shame" (compare Psalm 106:20; Jeremiah 2:11).
n.10: Hebrew *chatta't* means both "sin" and "sin offering": the priests eat the people's sin offerings (Leviticus 6:19, 6:26 in most English Bibles), and so profit from their sin.
n.11: Literally "they lift up his soul to their iniquity".
n.12: Literally "I will punish him for his ways and repay him for his deeds".
n.13: Literally "for they have abandoned the LORD to keep". Some join the first word of verse 11 to this verse: "they have abandoned the LORD to devote themselves to prostitution".
n.15: A wooden idol and a diviner's rod, used to seek omens.
n.16: Literally "they have prostituted themselves from under their God", as a wife leaves her husband's authority.
n.17: Hebrew *qedeshot*, "consecrated women". See Genesis 38:21 and Deuteronomy 23:18 (23:17 in most English Bibles).
n.18: Beth-aven, "house of wickedness", is a mocking name for Bethel, "house of God", where one of the royal shrines of the northern kingdom stood (1 Kings 12:28–33). Gilgal was another center of worship (9:15; 12:12, 12:11 in most English Bibles; Amos 4:4).
n.19: Or "Now the LORD will pasture them like a lamb in a broad meadow."
n.20: Ephraim, the largest tribe of the northern kingdom, is often used in Hosea as a name for the kingdom of Israel.
n.21: The Hebrew of this verse is very uncertain. *Her rulers* is literally "her shields".
n.22: Or "A spirit". Hebrew *ruach*. The wind will sweep them away (compare "a spirit of prostitution" in verse 12).
n.23: The same consonants can be read "because of their altars", as the Septuagint does.

v: Hear this, you priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Listen, house of the king! For the judgment is for you,[^1] because you have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread out on Tabor.
שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֨את הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים וְהַקְשִׁ֣יבוּ ׀ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּבֵ֤ית הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַאֲזִ֔ינוּ כִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם הַמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּֽי־פַח֙ הֱיִיתֶ֣ם לְמִצְפָּ֔ה וְרֶ֖שֶׁת פְּרוּשָׂ֥ה עַל־תָּבֽוֹר׃
The rebels have gone deep into slaughter,[^2] but I will discipline them all.[^3]
וְשַׁחֲטָ֥ה שֵׂטִ֖ים הֶעְמִ֑יקוּ וַאֲנִ֖י מוּסָ֥ר לְכֻלָּֽם׃
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. For now, Ephraim, you have prostituted yourself; Israel is defiled.
אֲנִי֙ יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹֽא־נִכְחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ הִזְנֵ֣יתָ אֶפְרַ֔יִם נִטְמָ֖א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Their deeds do not allow them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.[^4]
לֹ֤א יִתְּנוּ֙ מַ֣עַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם לָשׁ֖וּב אֶל־אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ זְנוּנִים֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔ם וְאֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃
Israel's pride testifies against him.[^5] Israel and Ephraim will stumble in their iniquity, and Judah also will stumble with them.
וְעָנָ֥ה גְאֽוֹן־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָנָ֑יו וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וְאֶפְרַ֗יִם יִכָּֽשְׁלוּ֙ בַּעֲוֺנָ֔ם כָּשַׁ֥ל גַּם־יְהוּדָ֖ה עִמָּֽם׃
With their flocks and their herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn from them.
בְּצֹאנָ֣ם וּבִבְקָרָ֗ם יֵֽ[m]לְכ֛וּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָ֑אוּ חָלַ֖ץ מֵהֶֽם׃
They have been unfaithful to the LORD, for they have borne children who are not his.[^6] Now the new moon[^7] will devour them along with their fields.
בַּיהוָ֣ה בָּגָ֔דוּ כִּֽי־בָנִ֥ים זָרִ֖ים יָלָ֑דוּ עַתָּ֛ה יֹאכְלֵ֥ם חֹ֖דֶשׁ אֶת־חֶלְקֵיהֶֽם׃ ס
Blow the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm in Beth-aven![^8] Behind you, Benjamin![^9]
תִּקְע֤וּ שׁוֹפָר֙ בַּגִּבְעָ֔ה חֲצֹצְרָ֖ה בָּרָמָ֑ה הָרִ֙יעוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אָ֔וֶן אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ בִּנְיָמִֽין׃
Ephraim will become a desolation on the day of punishment. Among the tribes of Israel I make known what is certain.
אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה בְּי֖וֹם תּֽוֹכֵחָ֑ה בְּשִׁבְטֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הוֹדַ֖עְתִּי נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃
The officials of Judah have become like those who move a boundary stone.[^10] I will pour out my fury on them like water.
הָיוּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה כְּמַסִּיגֵ֖י גְּב֑וּל עֲלֵיהֶ֕ם אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹךְ כַּמַּ֖יִם עֶבְרָתִֽי׃
Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment,[^11] because he was determined to follow a command.[^12]
עָשׁ֥וּק אֶפְרַ֖יִם רְצ֣וּץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֣י הוֹאִ֔יל הָלַ֖ךְ אַחֲרֵי־צָֽו׃
I am like a moth[^13] to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
וַאֲנִ֥י כָעָ֖שׁ לְאֶפְרָ֑יִם וְכָרָקָ֖ב לְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃
When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king.[^14] But he cannot heal you or cure you of your wound.
וַיַּ֨רְא אֶפְרַ֜יִם אֶת־חָלְי֗וֹ וִֽיהוּדָה֙ אֶת־מְזֹר֔וֹ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יָרֵ֑ב וְה֗וּא לֹ֤א יוּכַל֙ לִרְפֹּ֣א לָכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יִגְהֶ֥ה מִכֶּ֖ם מָזֽוֹר׃
For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue them.
כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֤י כַשַּׁ֙חַל֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם וְכַכְּפִ֖יר לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲנִ֨י אֲנִ֤י אֶטְרֹף֙ וְאֵלֵ֔ךְ אֶשָּׂ֖א וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃
I will go back to my place until they admit their guilt[^15] and seek my face. In their distress they will earnestly seek me.
אֵלֵ֤ךְ אָשׁ֙וּבָה֙ אֶל־מְקוֹמִ֔י עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר־יֶאְשְׁמ֖וּ וּבִקְשׁ֣וּ פָנָ֑י בַּצַּ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם יְשַׁחֲרֻֽנְנִי׃

n.1: Or "For you are responsible for justice". Hebrew *mishpat*.
n.2: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Some scholars read "they have dug deep the pit of Shittim", with small changes to the Hebrew, continuing the images of the snare and the net in verse 1.
n.3: Literally "and I am discipline for all of them".
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Or "a month", that is, very soon. The new moon was a festival (2:13, 2:11 in most English Bibles).
n.9: Perhaps a battle cry (compare Judges 5:14). Gibeah, Ramah and Bethel lay on the road north from Jerusalem, in the land of Benjamin.
n.10: Moving a neighbor's boundary stone was a serious crime (Deuteronomy 19:14; 27:17).
n.12: Hebrew *tsav*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "command" or a mocking syllable (compare Isaiah 28:10). The Septuagint reads "worthless things" (Hebrew *shav*).
n.14: The Hebrew as pointed reads *melekh yarev*, "King Jareb" or "a king who contends". The same consonants, divided differently, can be read *malki rav*, "the great king", a title of the kings of Assyria. Also in 10:6.

v: "Come, let us return to the LORD.[^1] For he has torn us, but he will heal us; he has struck us, but he will bind up our wounds.
לְכוּ֙ וְנָשׁ֣וּבָה אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י ה֥וּא טָרָ֖ף וְיִרְפָּאֵ֑נוּ יַ֖ךְ וְיַחְבְּשֵֽׁנוּ׃
After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, so that we may live before him.[^2]
יְחַיֵּ֖נוּ מִיֹּמָ֑יִם בַּיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יְקִמֵ֖נוּ וְנִחְיֶ֥ה לְפָנָֽיו׃
Let us know, let us press on to know the LORD. His coming is as sure as the dawn. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth."[^3]
וְנֵדְעָ֣ה נִרְדְּפָ֗ה לָדַ֙עַת֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כְּשַׁ֖חַר נָכ֣וֹן מֽוֹצָא֑וֹ וְיָב֤וֹא כַגֶּ֙שֶׁם֙ לָ֔נוּ כְּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ י֥וֹרֶה אָֽרֶץ׃
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your faithful love[^4] is like the morning mist, like the dew that goes away early.
מָ֤ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֙ אֶפְרַ֔יִם מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֖ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְחַסְדְּכֶם֙ כַּֽעֲנַן־בֹּ֔קֶר וְכַטַּ֖ל מַשְׁכִּ֥ים הֹלֵֽךְ׃
That is why I have cut them to pieces by the prophets; I have killed them by the words of my mouth, and my judgment goes out like light.[^5]
עַל־כֵּ֗ן חָצַ֙בְתִּי֙ בַּנְּבִיאִ֔ים הֲרַגְתִּ֖ים בְּאִמְרֵי־פִ֑י וּמִשְׁפָּטֶ֖יךָ א֥וֹר יֵצֵֽא׃
For I desire faithful love, not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.[^6]
כִּ֛י חֶ֥סֶד חָפַ֖צְתִּי וְלֹא־זָ֑בַח וְדַ֥עַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵעֹלֽוֹת׃
But like Adam they have broken the covenant;[^7] there they have been unfaithful to me.
וְהֵ֕מָּה כְּאָדָ֖ם עָבְר֣וּ בְרִ֑ית שָׁ֖ם בָּ֥גְדוּ בִֽי׃
Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with bloody footprints.
גִּלְעָ֕ד קִרְיַ֖ת פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן עֲקֻבָּ֖ה מִדָּֽם׃
As bands of robbers lie in wait for someone, so the company of priests murder on the road to Shechem.[^8] Indeed, they have committed shameful crimes.
וּכְחַכֵּ֨י אִ֜ישׁ גְּדוּדִ֗ים חֶ֚בֶר כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים דֶּ֖רֶךְ יְרַצְּחוּ־שֶׁ֑כְמָה כִּ֥י זִמָּ֖ה עָשֽׂוּ׃
In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing. Ephraim's prostitution is there; Israel is defiled.
בְּבֵית֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאִ֖יתִי *שעריריה **שַׁעֲרֽוּרִיָּ֑ה שָׁ֚ם זְנ֣וּת לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם נִטְמָ֖א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore the fortunes of my people.[^9]
גַּם־יְהוּדָ֕ה שָׁ֥ת קָצִ֖יר לָ֑ךְ בְּשׁוּבִ֖י שְׁב֥וּת עַמִּֽי׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Verses 1–3 give the words of the people who seek the LORD in their distress (5:15).
n.2: That is, soon. Some Christian writers have connected this verse with the resurrection of Jesus "on the third day" (1 Corinthians 15:4).
n.3: Hebrew *malqosh*, the spring rain of March and April, and *yoreh*, which can mean "the autumn rain" or "waters".
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*, loyal, covenant love. Also in verse 6.
n.5: The Hebrew as pointed reads "and your judgments, light goes out". The same consonants, divided differently, read "and my judgment goes out like light", as in the Septuagint.
n.6: The first half of the verse is quoted by Jesus in Matthew 9:13 and 12:7, following the Septuagint: "I desire mercy, not sacrifice."
n.7: Or "like human beings" or "at Adam". Adam was also a town in the Jordan valley (Joshua 3:16), which would explain "there".
n.8: The Hebrew of the first part of the verse is uncertain.
n.9: Many translations join this last clause to 7:1.

v: When I would heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim is exposed, and the wicked deeds of Samaria. For they practice deceit; a thief breaks in, and a band of raiders attacks in the street.
כְּרָפְאִ֣י לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְנִגְלָ֞ה עֲוֺ֤ן אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וְרָע֣וֹת שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י פָעֲל֖וּ שָׁ֑קֶר וְגַנָּ֣ב יָב֔וֹא פָּשַׁ֥ט גְּד֖וּד בַּחֽוּץ׃
But they do not consider[^1] that I remember all their wickedness. Now their deeds surround them; they are before my face.
וּבַל־יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ לִלְבָבָ֔ם כָּל־רָעָתָ֖ם זָכָ֑רְתִּי עַתָּה֙ סְבָב֣וּם מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם נֶ֥גֶד פָּנַ֖י הָיֽוּ׃
They make the king glad with their wickedness, and the officials with their lies.
בְּרָעָתָ֖ם יְשַׂמְּחוּ־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבְכַחֲשֵׁיהֶ֖ם שָׂרִֽים׃
They are all adulterers. They are like an oven heated by a baker, who stops stirring the fire from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.[^2]
כֻּלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים כְּמ֣וֹ תַנּ֔וּר בֹּעֵ֖רָה מֵֽאֹפֶ֑ה יִשְׁבּ֣וֹת מֵעִ֔יר מִלּ֥וּשׁ בָּצֵ֖ק עַד־חֻמְצָתֽוֹ׃
On the day of our king, the officials became sick with the heat of wine; he joined hands with mockers.[^3]
י֣וֹם מַלְכֵּ֔נוּ הֶחֱל֥וּ שָׂרִ֖ים חֲמַ֣ת מִיָּ֑יִן מָשַׁ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ אֶת־לֹצְצִֽים׃
For they draw near with their hearts like an oven in their plotting. All night their baker sleeps;[^4] in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
כִּֽי־קֵרְב֧וּ כַתַּנּ֛וּר לִבָּ֖ם בְּאָרְבָּ֑ם כָּל־הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ יָשֵׁ֣ן אֹֽפֵהֶ֔ם בֹּ֕קֶר ה֥וּא בֹעֵ֖ר כְּאֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָֽה׃
All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers.[^5] All their kings have fallen,[^6] and none of them calls on me.
כֻּלָּ֤ם יֵחַ֙מּוּ֙ כַּתַּנּ֔וּר וְאָכְל֖וּ אֶת־שֹֽׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם כָּל־מַלְכֵיהֶ֣ם נָפָ֔לוּ אֵין־קֹרֵ֥א בָהֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃
Ephraim mixes himself with the peoples. Ephraim is a flat cake not turned over.[^7]
אֶפְרַ֕יִם בָּעַמִּ֖ים ה֣וּא יִתְבּוֹלָ֑ל אֶפְרַ֛יִם הָיָ֥ה עֻגָ֖ה בְּלִ֥י הֲפוּכָֽה׃
Foreigners devour his strength, but he does not know it. Gray hair is sprinkled on him, but he does not know it.
אָכְל֤וּ זָרִים֙ כֹּח֔וֹ וְה֖וּא לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע גַּם־שֵׂיבָה֙ זָ֣רְקָה בּ֔וֹ וְה֖וּא לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃
Israel's pride testifies against him,[^8] yet they do not return to the LORD[^9] their God or seek him in spite of all this.
וְעָנָ֥ה גְאֽוֹן־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָנָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־שָׁ֙בוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א בִקְשֻׁ֖הוּ בְּכָל־זֹֽאת׃
Ephraim is like a dove, easily fooled and without sense.[^10] They call to Egypt; they go to Assyria.
וַיְהִ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם כְּיוֹנָ֥ה פוֹתָ֖ה אֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב מִצְרַ֥יִם קָרָ֖אוּ אַשּׁ֥וּר הָלָֽכוּ׃
As they go, I will spread my net over them; I will bring them down like the birds of the sky. I will discipline them according to the report to their assembly.[^11]
כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵלֵ֗כוּ אֶפְר֤וֹשׂ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ רִשְׁתִּ֔י כְּע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם אֽוֹרִידֵ֑ם אַיְסִרֵ֕ם כְּשֵׁ֖מַע לַעֲדָתָֽם׃ ס
Woe to them, for they have strayed from me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies about me.
א֤וֹי לָהֶם֙ כִּֽי־נָדְד֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נִּי שֹׁ֥ד לָהֶ֖ם כִּֽי־פָ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֑י וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶפְדֵּ֔ם וְהֵ֕מָּה דִּבְּר֥וּ עָלַ֖י כְּזָבִֽים׃
They do not cry out to me from their hearts when they wail on their beds. For grain and new wine they gather together;[^12] they turn away from me.
וְלֹֽא־זָעֲק֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בְּלִבָּ֔ם כִּ֥י יְיֵלִ֖ילוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם עַל־דָּגָ֧ן וְתִיר֛וֹשׁ יִתְגּוֹרָ֖רוּ יָס֥וּרוּ בִֽי׃
Though I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against me.
וַאֲנִ֣י יִסַּ֔רְתִּי חִזַּ֖קְתִּי זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑ם וְאֵלַ֖י יְחַשְּׁבוּ־רָֽע׃

They turn, but not to the Most High;[^13] they are like a faulty bow. Their officials will fall by the sword because of the insolence of their tongues. This will make them a laughingstock in the land of Egypt.
יָשׁ֣וּבוּ ׀ לֹ֣א עָ֗ל הָיוּ֙ כְּקֶ֣שֶׁת רְמִיָּ֔ה יִפְּל֥וּ בַחֶ֛רֶב שָׂרֵיהֶ֖ם מִזַּ֣עַם לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם ז֥וֹ לַעְגָּ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

n.1: Literally "they do not say to their hearts".
n.2: The Hebrew of verses 4–7 is difficult. The general picture is of conspirators whose passions smolder like a baker's oven until they flare up against their kings.
n.3: Literally "he drew his hand with mockers".
n.4: The same consonants can be read "their anger smolders".
n.6: Four of the last six kings of Israel were assassinated (2 Kings 15:10, 14, 25, 30).
n.7: That is, burned on one side and raw on the other.
n.9: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.11: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.12: Or "they drag themselves about". The Septuagint reads "they gash themselves" (compare 1 Kings 18:28), a Hebrew reading that differs by one letter.
n.13: Hebrew *lo al*, "not upward". *Al* may be a title of God, "the Most High" (compare 11:7). The meaning is uncertain.

v: Put the horn to your lips![^1] An eagle is over the house of the LORD,[^2] because they have broken my covenant and rebelled against my law.
אֶל־חִכְּךָ֣ שֹׁפָ֔ר כַּנֶּ֖שֶׁר עַל־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה יַ֚עַן עָבְר֣וּ בְרִיתִ֔י וְעַל־תּוֹרָתִ֖י פָּשָֽׁעוּ׃
They cry out to me, "My God, we, Israel, know you!"
לִ֖י יִזְעָ֑קוּ אֱלֹהַ֥י יְֽדַעֲנ֖וּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
זָנַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ט֑וֹב אוֹיֵ֖ב יִרְדְּֽפוֹ׃
They set up kings, but not through me; they appointed officials, but without my knowledge. With their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, so that they will be cut off.[^3]
הֵ֤ם הִמְלִיכוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מִמֶּ֔נִּי הֵשִׂ֖ירוּ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עְתִּי כַּסְפָּ֣ם וּזְהָבָ֗ם עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים לְמַ֖עַן יִכָּרֵֽת׃
He has rejected your calf, Samaria![^4] My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
זָנַח֙ עֶגְלֵ֣ךְ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן חָרָ֥ה אַפִּ֖י בָּ֑ם עַד־מָתַ֕י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ נִקָּיֹֽן׃
For it is from Israel! A craftsman made it; it is not God. The calf of Samaria will be broken to pieces.
כִּ֤י מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְה֔וּא חָרָ֣שׁ עָשָׂ֔הוּ וְלֹ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים ה֑וּא כִּֽי־שְׁבָבִ֣ים יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עֵ֖גֶל שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
For they sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind. The standing grain has no head; it will produce no flour.[^5] Even if it should produce, foreigners would swallow it up.
כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ יִזְרָ֖עוּ וְסוּפָ֣תָה יִקְצֹ֑רוּ קָמָ֣ה אֵֽין־ל֗וֹ צֶ֚מַח בְּלִ֣י יַֽעֲשֶׂה־קֶּ֔מַח אוּלַ֣י יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה זָרִ֖ים יִבְלָעֻֽהוּ׃
Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.[^6]
נִבְלַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַתָּה֙ הָי֣וּ בַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּכְלִ֖י אֵֽין־חֵ֥פֶץ בּֽוֹ׃
For they have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey wandering alone.[^7] Ephraim has hired lovers.[^8]
כִּֽי־הֵ֙מָּה֙ עָל֣וּ אַשּׁ֔וּר פֶּ֖רֶא בּוֹדֵ֣ד ל֑וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם הִתְנ֥וּ אֲהָבִֽים
Even though they hire them among the nations, I will now gather them together. Soon they will writhe[^9] under the burden of the king of princes.[^10]
גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־יִתְנ֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֖ם עַתָּ֣ה אֲקַבְּצֵ֑ם וַיָּחֵ֣לּוּ מְּעָ֔ט מִמַּשָּׂ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ שָׂרִֽים׃
Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, they have become to him altars for sinning.[^11]
כִּֽי־הִרְבָּ֥ה אֶפְרַ֛יִם מִזְבְּחֹ֖ת לַחֲטֹ֑א הָיוּ־ל֥וֹ מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לַחֲטֹֽא׃
Though I write for him the many things of my law,[^12] they are regarded as something strange.
*אכתוב־**אֶ֨כְתָּב־ל֔וֹ *רבו **רֻבֵּ֖י תּֽוֹרָתִ֑י כְּמוֹ־זָ֖ר נֶחְשָֽׁבוּ׃
They sacrifice meat as gifts to me[^13] and eat it, but the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins. They will return to Egypt.
זִבְחֵ֣י הַבְהָבַ֗י יִזְבְּח֤וּ בָשָׂר֙ וַיֹּאכֵ֔לוּ יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א רָצָ֑ם עַתָּ֞ה יִזְכֹּ֤ר עֲוֺנָם֙ וְיִפְקֹ֣ד חַטֹּאותָ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה מִצְרַ֥יִם יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃
Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces,[^14] and Judah has multiplied fortified cities. But I will send fire on his cities, and it will devour their strongholds.[^15]
וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־עֹשֵׂ֗הוּ וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ הֵֽיכָל֔וֹת וִֽיהוּדָ֕ה הִרְבָּ֖ה עָרִ֣ים בְּצֻר֑וֹת וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־אֵ֣שׁ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃ ס

n.1: Literally "To your palate the horn!" Hebrew *shofar*, a ram's horn blown as an alarm.
n.2: Literally "Like an eagle over the house of the LORD". Hebrew *nesher*, "eagle" or "vulture". *The house of the LORD* may here mean the land or people of Israel (compare 9:15). *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "so that it will be cut off", that is, the silver and gold, or Israel.
n.4: Or "Your calf is rejected, Samaria!" The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. The golden calves set up by Jeroboam I at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28–30) were the chief images of the northern kingdom, whose capital was Samaria.
n.5: A play on words: *tsemach*, "head of grain", and *qemach*, "flour".
n.6: Literally "like a vessel in which there is no pleasure".
n.8: Literally "Ephraim has given love-gifts". The same verb is used of paying a prostitute.
n.9: Or "Soon they will begin to dwindle". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.10: Probably the king of Assyria, who called himself "king of kings".
n.11: The altars that should have dealt with sin have become a means of sinning.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "ten thousand things of my law" but read "the many things of my law".
n.13: The meaning of the Hebrew *havhavay*, perhaps "my gifts", is uncertain.
n.15: Literally "her strongholds". The same words close the oracles of Amos 1:4–2:5.

v: Do not rejoice, Israel; do not exult like the peoples. For you have prostituted yourself and left your God.[^1] You have loved a prostitute's wages on every threshing floor of grain.
אַל־תִּשְׂמַ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל ׀ אֶל־גִּיל֙ כָּֽעַמִּ֔ים כִּ֥י זָנִ֖יתָ מֵעַ֣ל אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אָהַ֣בְתָּ אֶתְנָ֔ן עַ֖ל כָּל־גָּרְנ֥וֹת דָּגָֽן׃
Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail her.
גֹּ֥רֶן וָיֶ֖קֶב לֹ֣א יִרְעֵ֑ם וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ יְכַ֥חֶשׁ בָּֽהּ׃
They will not remain in the land of the LORD.[^2] Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.
לֹ֥א יֵשְׁב֖וּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁ֤ב אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבְאַשּׁ֖וּר טָמֵ֥א יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please him. They will be like the bread of mourners to them; all who eat it will be defiled.[^3] For their bread will be for themselves alone;[^4] it will not come into the house of the LORD.
לֹא־יִסְּכ֨וּ לַיהוָ֥ה ׀ יַיִן֮ וְלֹ֣א יֶֽעֶרְבוּ־לוֹ֒ זִבְחֵיהֶ֗ם כְּלֶ֤חֶם אוֹנִים֙ לָהֶ֔ם כָּל־אֹכְלָ֖יו יִטַמָּ֑אוּ כִּֽי־לַחְמָ֣ם לְנַפְשָׁ֔ם לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
What will you do on the day of the appointed festival, on the day of the LORD's feast?
מַֽה־תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ לְי֣וֹם מוֹעֵ֑ד וּלְי֖וֹם חַג־יְהוָֽה׃

For look, they have gone away from destruction, but Egypt will gather them, and Memphis[^5] will bury them. Nettles will take possession of their precious things of silver, and thorns will grow in their tents.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה הָֽלְכוּ֙ מִשֹּׁ֔ד מִצְרַ֥יִם תְּקַבְּצֵ֖ם מֹ֣ף תְּקַבְּרֵ֑ם מַחְמַ֣ד לְכַסְפָּ֗ם קִמּוֹשׂ֙ יִֽירָשֵׁ֔ם ח֖וֹחַ בְּאָהֳלֵיהֶֽם׃

The days of punishment have come; the days of repayment have come. Let Israel know it! "The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad!"[^6] So it is because of your great iniquity, and your hostility is great.
בָּ֣אוּ ׀ יְמֵ֣י הַפְּקֻדָּ֗ה בָּ֚אוּ יְמֵ֣י הַשִׁלֻּ֔ם יֵדְע֖וּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֱוִ֣יל הַנָּבִ֗יא מְשֻׁגָּע֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָר֔וּחַ עַ֚ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנְךָ֔ וְרַבָּ֖ה מַשְׂטֵמָֽה׃
The prophet is a watchman over Ephraim with my God,[^7] yet a fowler's snare is on all his ways, and hostility in the house of his God.
צֹפֶ֥ה אֶפְרַ֖יִם עִם־אֱלֹהָ֑י נָבִ֞יא פַּ֤ח יָקוֹשׁ֙ עַל־כָּל־דְּרָכָ֔יו מַשְׂטֵמָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Gibeah.[^8] He will remember their iniquity; he will punish their sins.
הֶעְמִֽיקוּ־שִׁחֵ֖תוּ כִּימֵ֣י הַגִּבְעָ֑ה יִזְכּ֣וֹר עֲוֺנָ֔ם יִפְק֖וֹד חַטֹּאותָֽם׃ ס

Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your ancestors. But they came to Baal-peor[^9] and dedicated themselves to the Shameful Thing,[^10] and they became detestable, like the thing they loved.

כַּעֲנָבִ֣ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר מָצָ֙אתִי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּבִכּוּרָ֤ה בִתְאֵנָה֙ בְּרֵ֣אשִׁיתָ֔הּ רָאִ֖יתִי אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם הֵ֜מָּה בָּ֣אוּ בַֽעַל־פְּע֗וֹר וַיִּנָּֽזְרוּ֙ לַבֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיִּהְי֥וּ שִׁקּוּצִ֖ים כְּאָהֳבָֽם׃
Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird: no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
אֶפְרַ֕יִם כָּע֖וֹף יִתְעוֹפֵ֣ף כְּבוֹדָ֑ם מִלֵּדָ֥ה וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן וּמֵהֵרָיֽוֹן׃
Even if they raise children, I will bereave them until no one is left. Woe to them indeed when I turn away from them!
כִּ֤י אִם־יְגַדְּלוּ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וְשִׁכַּלְתִּ֖ים מֵֽאָדָ֑ם כִּֽי־גַם־א֥וֹי לָהֶ֖ם בְּשׂוּרִ֥י מֵהֶֽם׃
Ephraim, as I saw, was like Tyre, planted in a pleasant meadow; but Ephraim will bring out his children to the slayer.[^11]
אֶפְרַ֛יִם כַּאֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֥יתִי לְצ֖וֹר שְׁתוּלָ֣ה בְנָוֶ֑ה וְאֶפְרַ֕יִם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶל־הֹרֵ֖ג בָּנָֽיו׃
Give them, LORD—what will you give? Give them a womb that miscarries and breasts that are dry.
תֵּן־לָהֶ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מַה־תִּתֵּ֑ן תֵּן־לָהֶם֙ רֶ֣חֶם מַשְׁכִּ֔יל וְשָׁדַ֖יִם צֹמְקִֽים׃
All their wickedness is in Gilgal; there I came to hate them. Because of their wicked deeds I will drive them out of my house. I will love them no more; all their officials are rebels.[^12]
כָּל־רָעָתָ֤ם בַּגִּלְגָּל֙ כִּֽי־שָׁ֣ם שְׂנֵאתִ֔ים עַ֚ל רֹ֣עַ מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם מִבֵּיתִ֖י אֲגָרְשֵׁ֑ם לֹ֤א אוֹסֵף֙ אַהֲבָתָ֔ם כָּל־שָׂרֵיהֶ֖ם סֹרְרִֽים׃
Ephraim is struck down; their root is dried up; they will bear no fruit.[^13] Even if they give birth, I will kill the precious offspring of their womb.
הֻכָּ֣ה אֶפְרַ֔יִם שָׁרְשָׁ֥ם יָבֵ֖שׁ פְּרִ֣י *בלי־**בַֽל־יַעֲשׂ֑וּן גַּ֚ם כִּ֣י יֵֽלֵד֔וּן וְהֵמַתִּ֖י מַחֲמַדֵּ֥י בִטְנָֽם׃ ס
My God will reject them, because they have not listened to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.
יִמְאָסֵ֣ם אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ ל֑וֹ וְיִהְי֥וּ נֹדְדִ֖ים בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃ ס

n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Food in a house of mourning was unclean because of contact with the dead (Numbers 19:14–15; Deuteronomy 26:14).
n.4: Literally "for their soul" or "for their appetite".
n.5: Hebrew *Moph*, Memphis, the ancient capital of Lower Egypt, famous for its tombs.
n.6: Probably the people's mockery of the prophet. The words could also be the prophet's own verdict on false prophets.
n.7: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.9: See Numbers 25:1–9. The god Baal of Peor was worshiped in Moab.
n.10: Hebrew *boshet*, "shame", a word that later scribes and prophets put in place of the name Baal (compare Jeremiah 3:24; 11:13).
n.11: The meaning of the Hebrew of the first half of the verse is uncertain. The Septuagint reads "Ephraim, as I saw, has given up his children as prey", which differs by one letter (*le-tsayid*, "for prey", for *le-tsor*, "like Tyre").
n.12: A play on words: *sarehem*, "their officials", and *sorerim*, "rebels".

v: Israel is a luxuriant vine[^1] that yields its fruit. The more his fruit increased, the more altars he built; the better his land became, the finer he made his standing stones.[^2]
גֶּ֤פֶן בּוֹקֵק֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל פְּרִ֖י יְשַׁוֶּה־לּ֑וֹ כְּרֹ֣ב לְפִרְי֗וֹ הִרְבָּה֙ לַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת כְּט֣וֹב לְאַרְצ֔וֹ הֵיטִ֖יבוּ מַצֵּבֽוֹת׃
Their heart is false;[^3] now they must bear their guilt. He will break down their altars and destroy their standing stones.
חָלַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם עַתָּ֣ה יֶאְשָׁ֑מוּ ה֚וּא יַעֲרֹ֣ף מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֔ם יְשֹׁדֵ֖ד מַצֵּבוֹתָֽם׃
For now they will say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD.[^4] And the king, what could he do for us?"
כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ לָ֑נוּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָרֵ֙אנוּ֙ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־יַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לָּֽנוּ׃
They speak mere words, swear empty oaths and make covenants. So lawsuits spring up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.
דִּבְּר֣וּ דְבָרִ֔ים אָל֥וֹת שָׁ֖וְא כָּרֹ֣ת בְּרִ֑ית וּפָרַ֤ח כָּרֹאשׁ֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט עַ֖ל תַּלְמֵ֥י שָׂדָֽי׃

The inhabitants of Samaria fear for the calf[^5] of Beth-aven.[^6] Its people mourn over it, and its idolatrous priests[^7] wail[^8] over it, over its glory, because it has gone into exile from them.[^9]
לְעֶגְלוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית אָ֔וֶן יָג֖וּרוּ שְׁכַ֣ן שֹֽׁמְר֑וֹן כִּי־אָבַ֨ל עָלָ֜יו עַמּ֗וֹ וּכְמָרָיו֙ עָלָ֣יו יָגִ֔ילוּ עַל־כְּבוֹד֖וֹ כִּֽי־גָלָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
It too will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king.[^10] Ephraim will be put to shame, and Israel will be ashamed of his own plans.
גַּם־אוֹתוֹ֙ לְאַשּׁ֣וּר יוּבָ֔ל מִנְחָ֖ה לְמֶ֣לֶךְ יָרֵ֑ב בָּשְׁנָה֙ אֶפְרַ֣יִם יִקָּ֔ח וְיֵב֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעֲצָתֽוֹ׃
Samaria and her king will be cut off[^11] like a twig on the surface of the water.
נִדְמֶ֥ה שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מַלְכָּ֑הּ כְּקֶ֖צֶף עַל־פְּנֵי־מָֽיִם׃

The high places of Aven,[^12] the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. Thorns and thistles will grow up over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, "Cover us!" and to the hills, "Fall on us!"[^13]
וְנִשְׁמְד֞וּ בָּמ֣וֹת אָ֗וֶן חַטַּאת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ק֣וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֔ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֑ם וְאָמְר֤וּ לֶֽהָרִים֙ כַּסּ֔וּנוּ וְלַגְּבָע֖וֹת נִפְל֥וּ עָלֵֽינוּ׃ ס
Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel.[^14] There they have remained. Will not war overtake them in Gibeah, war against the wicked?[^15]
מִימֵי֙ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה חָטָ֖אתָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל שָׁ֣ם עָמָ֔דוּ לֹֽא־תַשִּׂיגֵ֧ם בַּגִּבְעָ֛ה מִלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־בְּנֵ֥י עַֽלְוָֽה׃
When I choose, I will discipline them. Nations will be gathered against them, when they are bound for their double iniquity.[^16]
בְּאַוָּתִ֖י וְאֶסֳּרֵ֑ם וְאֻסְּפ֤וּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ עַמִּ֔ים בְּאָסְרָ֖ם לִשְׁתֵּ֥י *עינתם **עוֹנֹתָֽם׃
Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, and I spared her fair neck.[^17] But now I will harness Ephraim; Judah must plow; Jacob must harrow for himself.
וְאֶפְרַ֜יִם עֶגְלָ֤ה מְלֻמָּדָה֙ אֹהַ֣בְתִּי לָד֔וּשׁ וַאֲנִ֣י עָבַ֔רְתִּי עַל־ט֖וּב צַוָּארָ֑הּ אַרְכִּ֤יב אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ יַחֲר֣וֹשׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה יְשַׂדֶּד־ל֖וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap the fruit of faithful love.[^18] Break up your unplowed ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.[^19]
זִרְע֨וּ לָכֶ֤ם לִצְדָקָה֙ קִצְר֣וּ לְפִי־חֶ֔סֶד נִ֥ירוּ לָכֶ֖ם נִ֑יר וְעֵת֙ לִדְר֣וֹשׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה עַד־יָב֕וֹא וְיֹרֶ֥ה צֶ֖דֶק לָכֶֽם׃
You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in the great number of your warriors,
חֲרַשְׁתֶּם־רֶ֛שַׁע עַוְלָ֥תָה קְצַרְתֶּ֖ם אֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם פְּרִי־כָ֑חַשׁ כִּֽי־בָטַ֥חְתָּ בְדַרְכְּךָ֖ בְּרֹ֥ב גִּבּוֹרֶֽיךָ׃

the roar of battle will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel on the day of battle,[^20] when mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.
וְקָ֣אם שָׁאוֹן֮ בְּעַמֶּךָ֒ וְכָל־מִבְצָרֶ֣יךָ יוּשַּׁ֔ד כְּשֹׁ֧ד שַֽׁלְמַ֛ן בֵּ֥ית אַֽרְבֵ֖אל בְּי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה אֵ֥ם עַל־בָּנִ֖ים רֻטָּֽשָׁה׃
This is what Bethel will do to you,[^21] because of your great wickedness.[^22] At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
כָּ֗כָה עָשָׂ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל מִפְּנֵ֖י רָעַ֣ת רָֽעַתְכֶ֑ם בַּשַּׁ֕חַר נִדְמֹ֥ה נִדְמָ֖ה מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

n.1: Hebrew *boqeq*, which usually means "laid waste" or "emptied"; here perhaps "spreading" or "luxuriant".
n.2: Hebrew *matsevot*, standing stones set up as objects of worship. Also in verse 2.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Hebrew plural, "heifers", perhaps said in mockery. See 8:5.
n.7: Hebrew *kemarim*, a word used only of priests of other gods (2 Kings 23:5; Zephaniah 1:4).
n.8: Hebrew *yagilu*, which usually means "rejoice"; here perhaps the shouts of a ritual of lament.
n.9: Compare 1 Samuel 4:21–22, "The glory has gone into exile from Israel."
n.15: Literally "against the sons of wickedness". The Hebrew *alvah* is an unusual form of *avlah*, "wickedness".
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "their two springs" or "their two eyes" but read "their double iniquity".
n.17: Literally "I passed over the goodness of her neck". Or "I put a yoke on her fair neck". Threshing was light work, and an ox treading out grain was free to eat (Deuteronomy 25:4).
n.18: Literally "reap according to faithful love". Hebrew *chesed*, loyal, covenant love.
n.19: Or "teaches you righteousness". The Hebrew verb *yarah* can mean "to rain" or "to teach".
n.20: Shalman and Beth-arbel are not otherwise known. Shalman may be Shalmaneser V of Assyria (2 Kings 17:3) or Salamanu, a king of Moab named in Assyrian records.
n.21: Or "So it will be done to you, Bethel". The Septuagint reads "house of Israel".

v: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.[^1]
כִּ֛י נַ֥עַר יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וָאֹהֲבֵ֑הוּ וּמִמִּצְרַ֖יִם קָרָ֥אתִי לִבְנִֽי׃
The more they were called, the more they went away from them.[^2] They kept sacrificing to the Baals and burning incense to carved images.
קָרְא֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם כֵּ֚ן הָלְכ֣וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם לַבְּעָלִ֣ים יְזַבֵּ֔חוּ וְלַפְּסִלִ֖ים יְקַטֵּרֽוּן׃
Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by their arms,[^3] but they did not know that I healed them.
וְאָנֹכִ֤י תִרְגַּ֙לְתִּי֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם קָחָ֖ם עַל־זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כִּ֥י רְפָאתִֽים׃
I led them with cords of human kindness,[^4] with bands of love. I was to them like those who lift a yoke from their jaws,[^5] and I bent down to them and fed them.
בְּחַבְלֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶמְשְׁכֵם֙ בַּעֲבֹת֣וֹת אַהֲבָ֔ה וָאֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם כִּמְרִ֥ימֵי עֹ֖ל עַ֣ל לְחֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו אוֹכִֽיל׃
He will not return to the land of Egypt,[^6] but Assyria will be his king, because they refused to return to me.[^7]
לֹ֤א יָשׁוּב֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאַשּׁ֖וּר ה֣וּא מַלְכּ֑וֹ כִּ֥י מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃
The sword will whirl through his cities; it will destroy the bars of his gates[^8] and devour them because of their schemes.
וְחָלָ֥ה חֶ֙רֶב֙ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְכִלְּתָ֥ה בַדָּ֖יו וְאָכָ֑לָה מִֽמֹּעֲצ֖וֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
My people are bent on turning away from me. They call him upward, but he will not raise them up at all.[^9]
וְעַמִּ֥י תְלוּאִ֖ים לִמְשֽׁוּבָתִ֑י וְאֶל־עַל֙ יִקְרָאֻ֔הוּ יַ֖חַד לֹ֥א יְרוֹמֵם׃

How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboiim?[^10] My heart is turned over within me; all my compassion is stirred.[^11]
אֵ֞יךְ אֶתֶּנְךָ֣ אֶפְרַ֗יִם אֲמַגֶּנְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֚יךְ אֶתֶּנְךָ֣ כְאַדְמָ֔ה אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כִּצְבֹאיִ֑ם נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ עָלַי֙ לִבִּ֔י יַ֖חַד נִכְמְר֥וּ נִחוּמָֽי׃
I will not carry out my burning anger; I will not again destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not a human being, the Holy One among you, and I will not come in wrath.[^12]
לֹ֤א אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ חֲר֣וֹן אַפִּ֔י לֹ֥א אָשׁ֖וּב לְשַׁחֵ֣ת אֶפְרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל אָֽנֹכִי֙ וְלֹא־אִ֔ישׁ בְּקִרְבְּךָ֣ קָד֔וֹשׁ וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וֹא בְּעִֽיר׃
They will follow the LORD;[^13] he will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.[^14]
אַחֲרֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה יֵלְכ֖וּ כְּאַרְיֵ֣ה יִשְׁאָ֑ג כִּֽי־ה֣וּא יִשְׁאַ֔ג וְיֶחֶרְד֥וּ בָנִ֖ים מִיָּֽם׃
They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from the land of Assyria, and I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.
יֶחֶרְד֤וּ כְצִפּוֹר֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וּכְיוֹנָ֖ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְהוֹשַׁבְתִּ֥ים עַל־בָּתֵּיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Quoted in Matthew 2:15, which follows the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads "and out of Egypt I called his children".
n.2: Literally "They called to them; so they went from before them", perhaps meaning the prophets (verse 7; 12:11, 12:10 in most English Bibles). The Septuagint reads "The more I called them, the more they went away from me".
n.3: Literally "he took them on his arms". The Septuagint and the Vulgate read "I took them in my arms".
n.5: Or "like those who lift a little child to their cheek", reading the same consonants as *ul*, "infant", instead of *ol*, "yoke".
n.6: Or "Will he not return to the land of Egypt?" Elsewhere Hosea says that Ephraim will return to Egypt (8:13; 9:3).
n.7: "To me" is supplied. Literally "they refused to return".
n.8: Literally "his bars". Some take the word to mean "his boasters" or "his false prophets".
n.9: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. *Upward* (Hebrew *al*) may be a title of God, "the Most High" (compare 7:16).
n.10: Admah and Zeboiim were destroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 14:2; Deuteronomy 29:22, 29:23 in most English Bibles).
n.12: Or "I will not come into the city". The Hebrew *be-ir* usually means "into a city".
n.13: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.

v: Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit.[^1] But Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.[^2]
סְבָבֻ֤נִי בְכַ֙חַשׁ֙ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וּבְמִרְמָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה עֹ֥ד רָד֙ עִם־אֵ֔ל וְעִם־קְדוֹשִׁ֖ים נֶאֱמָֽן׃
Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long. He multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and olive oil is carried to Egypt.
אֶפְרַ֜יִם רֹעֶ֥ה ר֙וּחַ֙ וְרֹדֵ֣ף קָדִ֔ים כָּל־הַיּ֕וֹם כָּזָ֥ב וָשֹׁ֖ד יַרְבֶּ֑ה וּבְרִית֙ עִם־אַשּׁ֣וּר יִכְרֹ֔תוּ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן לְמִצְרַ֥יִם יוּבָֽל׃
The LORD[^3] has a case against Judah; he will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
וְרִ֥יב לַֽיהוָ֖ה עִם־יְהוּדָ֑ה וְלִפְקֹ֤ד עַֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כְּמַעֲלָלָ֖יו יָשִׁ֥יב לֽוֹ׃
In the womb he grasped his brother's heel,[^4] and in his manhood he struggled with God.[^5]
בַּבֶּ֖טֶן עָקַ֣ב אֶת־אָחִ֑יו וּבְאוֹנ֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ה אֶת־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
He struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us.[^6]
וַיָּ֤שַׂר אֶל־מַלְאָךְ֙ וַיֻּכָ֔ל בָּכָ֖ה וַיִּתְחַנֶּן־ל֑וֹ בֵּֽית־אֵל֙ יִמְצָאֶ֔נּוּ וְשָׁ֖ם יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּֽנוּ׃
The LORD, the God of Armies,[^7] the LORD is his name![^8]
וַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַצְּבָא֑וֹת יְהוָ֖ה זִכְרֽוֹ׃
As for you, return to your God with his help.[^9] Keep faithful love[^10] and justice, and wait for your God continually.
וְאַתָּ֖ה בֵּאלֹהֶ֣יךָ תָשׁ֑וּב חֶ֤סֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט֙ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְקַוֵּ֥ה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ תָּמִֽיד׃
A merchant,[^11] in whose hands are false scales, he loves to oppress.
כְּנַ֗עַן בְּיָד֛וֹ מֹאזְנֵ֥י מִרְמָ֖ה לַעֲשֹׁ֥ק אָהֵֽב׃
Ephraim says, "Surely I have become rich; I have found wealth for myself.[^12] In all my labor they will find in me no iniquity that is sin."
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶפְרַ֔יִם אַ֣ךְ עָשַׁ֔רְתִּי מָצָ֥אתִי א֖וֹן לִ֑י כָּל־יְגִיעַ֕י לֹ֥א יִמְצְאוּ־לִ֖י עָוֺ֥ן אֲשֶׁר־חֵֽטְא׃
But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt.[^13] I will make you live in tents again, as in the days of the appointed festival.[^14]
וְאָנֹכִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עֹ֛ד אוֹשִֽׁיבְךָ֥ בָ[t]אֳהָלִ֖ים כִּימֵ֥י מוֹעֵֽד׃
I spoke to the prophets; it was I who multiplied visions, and through the prophets I spoke in parables.[^15]
וְדִבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ עַל־הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים וְאָנֹכִ֖י חָז֣וֹן הִרְבֵּ֑יתִי וּבְיַ֥ד הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֲדַמֶּֽה׃
If Gilead is wicked,[^16] surely they are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars will be like heaps of stones[^17] in the furrows of a field.
אִם־גִּלְעָ֥ד אָ֙וֶן֙ אַךְ־שָׁ֣וְא הָי֔וּ בַּגִּלְגָּ֖ל שְׁוָרִ֣ים זִבֵּ֑חוּ גַּ֤ם מִזְבְּחוֹתָם֙ כְּגַלִּ֔ים עַ֖ל תַּלְמֵ֥י שָׂדָֽי׃
Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.[^18]
וַיִּבְרַ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׂדֵ֣ה אֲרָ֑ם וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ד יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבְאִשָּׁ֖ה שָׁמָֽר׃
By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet Israel was kept.[^19]
וּבְנָבִ֕יא הֶעֱלָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּבְנָבִ֖יא נִשְׁמָֽר׃
Ephraim has provoked bitter anger, so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt on him and repay him for his contempt.
הִכְעִ֥יס אֶפְרַ֖יִם תַּמְרוּרִ֑ים וְדָמָיו֙ עָלָ֣יו יִטּ֔וֹשׁ וְחֶ֨רְפָּת֔וֹ יָשִׁ֥יב ל֖וֹ אֲדֹנָֽיו׃

n.1: This verse is 11:12 in most English Bibles, and verses 2–15 are 12:1–14.
n.2: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. It may also mean "and Judah is still unruly against God, against the faithful Holy One". *Holy One* is plural in Hebrew, probably a plural of majesty (compare Proverbs 9:10; 30:3), or "the holy ones".
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: A play on words: *aqav*, "he grasped the heel", and *Ya'aqov*, "Jacob" (Genesis 25:26; 27:36).
n.5: A play on words: *sarah*, "he struggled", and *Yisra'el*, "Israel" (Genesis 32:25–29, 32:24–28 in most English Bibles). Also in verse 5.
n.6: The Septuagint and the Syriac read "with him". On Jacob at Bethel, see Genesis 28:10–22; 35:1–15.
n.7: *The LORD, the God of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH Elohei ha-tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD God of hosts". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.8: Literally "The LORD is his memorial", the name by which he is to be remembered (Exodus 3:15).
n.9: Literally "by your God you will return".
n.13: That is, since the time of the exodus. Also in 13:4.
n.14: Probably the Festival of Shelters, when the Israelites lived in shelters to remember the wilderness (Leviticus 23:42–43).
n.15: Or "and through the prophets I will bring destruction". The Hebrew verb can have either meaning.
n.16: Hebrew *aven*, "wickedness", the word used in the mocking name Beth-aven (4:15).
n.17: A play on words: *Gilgal* and *gallim*, "heaps of stones".
n.18: See Genesis 28:5; 29:15–30. *Kept* (Hebrew *shamar*) is the same verb as in verse 14.

v: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal and died.
כְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ רְתֵ֔ת נָשָׂ֥א ה֖וּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֶּאְשַׁ֥ם בַּבַּ֖עַל וַיָּמֹֽת׃

Now they sin more and more. They make for themselves cast images from their silver, idols skillfully made,[^1] all of them the work of craftsmen. They say of them, "Let those who sacrifice kiss calves!"[^2]
וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ יוֹסִ֣פוּ לַחֲטֹ֗א וַיַּעְשׂ֣וּ לָהֶם֩ מַסֵּכָ֨ה מִכַּסְפָּ֤ם כִּתְבוּנָם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חָרָשִׁ֖ים כֻּלֹּ֑ה לָהֶם֙ הֵ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים זֹבְחֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם עֲגָלִ֖ים יִשָּׁקֽוּן׃
Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the dew that goes away early, like chaff that swirls from a threshing floor, like smoke from a window.[^3]
לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיוּ֙ כַּעֲנַן־בֹּ֔קֶר וְכַטַּ֖ל מַשְׁכִּ֣ים הֹלֵ֑ךְ כְּמֹץ֙ יְסֹעֵ֣ר מִגֹּ֔רֶן וּכְעָשָׁ֖ן מֵאֲרֻבָּֽה׃
But I am the LORD[^4] your God from the land of Egypt.[^5] You know no God but me, and there is no savior except me.
וְאָנֹכִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וֵאלֹהִ֤ים זֽוּלָתִי֙ לֹ֣א תֵדָ֔ע וּמוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אַ֖יִן בִּלְתִּֽי׃
It was I who knew you[^6] in the wilderness, in the land of drought.
אֲנִ֥י יְדַעְתִּ֖יךָ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ תַּלְאֻבֽוֹת׃
When they had pasture, they were filled; they were filled, and their hearts were lifted up. That is why they forgot me.
כְּמַרְעִיתָם֙ וַיִּשְׂבָּ֔עוּ שָׂבְע֖וּ וַיָּ֣רָם לִבָּ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֖ן שְׁכֵחֽוּנִי׃
So I will be like a lion to them; like a leopard I will lurk by the road.[^7]
וָאֱהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם כְּמוֹ־שָׁ֑חַל כְּנָמֵ֖ר עַל־דֶּ֥רֶךְ אָשֽׁוּר׃
I will meet them like a bear robbed of her cubs, and I will tear open their chests.[^8] There I will devour them like a lioness; the wild animals will rip them apart.
אֶפְגְּשֵׁם֙ כְּדֹ֣ב שַׁכּ֔וּל וְאֶקְרַ֖ע סְג֣וֹר לִבָּ֑ם וְאֹכְלֵ֥ם שָׁם֙ כְּלָבִ֔יא חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה תְּבַקְּעֵֽם׃
It is your destruction, Israel, that you are against me, against your helper.[^9]
שִֽׁחֶתְךָ֥ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּֽי־בִ֥י בְעֶזְרֶֽךָ׃
Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities? And where are your rulers,[^10] of whom you said, "Give me a king and officials"?
אֱהִ֤י מַלְכְּךָ֙ אֵפ֔וֹא וְיוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֖ בְּכָל־עָרֶ֑יךָ וְשֹׁ֣פְטֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתָּ תְּנָה־לִּ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ וְשָׂרִֽים׃
I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my wrath.
אֶֽתֶּן־לְךָ֥ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י וְאֶקַּ֖ח בְּעֶבְרָתִֽי׃ ס
Ephraim's iniquity is bound up; his sin is stored away.
צָרוּר֙ עֲוֺ֣ן אֶפְרָ֔יִם צְפוּנָ֖ה חַטָּאתֽוֹ׃
The pains of childbirth come on him, but he is an unwise child, for when the time comes he does not present himself at the opening of the womb.[^11]
חֶבְלֵ֥י יֽוֹלֵדָ֖ה יָבֹ֣אוּ ל֑וֹ הוּא־בֵן֙ לֹ֣א חָכָ֔ם כִּֽי־עֵ֥ת לֹֽא־יַעֲמֹ֖ד בְּמִשְׁבַּ֥ר בָּנִֽים׃
Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol? Shall I redeem them from death? Where, O death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your destruction?[^12] Compassion is hidden from my eyes.
מִיַּ֤ד שְׁאוֹל֙ אֶפְדֵּ֔ם מִמָּ֖וֶת אֶגְאָלֵ֑ם אֱהִ֨י דְבָרֶיךָ֜ מָ֗וֶת אֱהִ֤י קָֽטָבְךָ֙ שְׁא֔וֹל נֹ֖חַם יִסָּתֵ֥ר מֵעֵינָֽי׃

Though he flourishes among his brothers,[^13] an east wind will come, the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness. His spring will dry up, and his fountain will fail. He will plunder his treasury of every precious thing.[^14]
כִּ֣י ה֔וּא בֵּ֥ן אַחִ֖ים יַפְרִ֑יא יָב֣וֹא קָדִים֩ ר֨וּחַ יְהוָ֜ה מִמִּדְבָּ֣ר עֹלֶ֗ה וְיֵב֤וֹשׁ מְקוֹרוֹ֙ וְיֶחֱרַ֣ב מַעְיָנ֔וֹ ה֣וּא יִשְׁסֶ֔ה אוֹצַ֖ר כָּל־כְּלִ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה׃

n.2: Or "People who offer human sacrifice kiss calves!" Literally "sacrificers of humankind kiss calves". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. On kissing an idol, compare 1 Kings 19:18.
n.3: An opening in the roof or wall through which smoke escaped.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: The Septuagint reads "I shepherded you", a Hebrew reading that differs by one letter.
n.7: Hebrew *ashur*, "I will watch", is spelled like *Ashur*, "Assyria".
n.9: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.11: Literally "the breaking forth of children". The child who will not be born is a picture of Ephraim's refusal to change.
n.12: Or "I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from death." The Hebrew has no marker of a question. *Ehi*, "where?", can also be read "I will be": "I will be your plagues, O death; I will be your destruction, O Sheol." *Sheol* is the realm of the dead. Paul adapts the second half in 1 Corinthians 15:55, close to the Septuagint: "Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?"
n.13: A play on words: *yafri*, "flourishes", and *Ephraim*. Or "among the reeds".
n.14: *He* is probably the conqueror whom the east wind represents.

v: Samaria will bear her guilt, because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.[^1]
תֶּאְשַׁם֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י מָרְתָ֖ה בֵּֽאלֹהֶ֑יהָ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ עֹלְלֵיהֶ֣ם יְרֻטָּ֔שׁוּ וְהָרִיּוֹתָ֖יו יְבֻקָּֽעוּ׃ פ
Return, Israel, to the LORD[^2] your God, for you have stumbled because of your iniquity.
שׁ֚וּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֥י כָשַׁ֖לְתָּ בַּעֲוֺנֶֽךָ׃
Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him, "Take away all iniquity and accept what is good, and we will offer our lips as bulls.[^3]
קְח֤וּ עִמָּכֶם֙ דְּבָרִ֔ים וְשׁ֖וּבוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה אִמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כָּל־תִּשָּׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְקַח־ט֔וֹב וּֽנְשַׁלְּמָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים שְׂפָתֵֽינוּ׃
Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses. We will never again say 'Our God' to the work of our hands, for in you the orphan finds compassion."
אַשּׁ֣וּר ׀ לֹ֣א יוֹשִׁיעֵ֗נוּ עַל־סוּס֙ לֹ֣א נִרְכָּ֔ב וְלֹא־נֹ֥אמַר ע֛וֹד אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁר־בְּךָ֖ יְרֻחַ֥ם יָתֽוֹם׃
I will heal their unfaithfulness; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from him.
אֶרְפָּא֙ מְשׁ֣וּבָתָ֔ם אֹהֲבֵ֖ם נְדָבָ֑ה כִּ֛י שָׁ֥ב אַפִּ֖י מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily,[^4] and he will strike roots like Lebanon.[^5]
אֶהְיֶ֤ה כַטַּל֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִפְרַ֖ח כַּשּֽׁוֹשַׁנָּ֑ה וְיַ֥ךְ שָׁרָשָׁ֖יו כַּלְּבָנֽוֹן׃
His shoots will spread out; his splendor will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
יֵֽלְכוּ֙ יֹֽנְקוֹתָ֔יו וִיהִ֥י כַזַּ֖יִת הוֹד֑וֹ וְרֵ֥יחַֽ ל֖וֹ כַּלְּבָנֽוֹן׃
Those who live in his shade will return. They will flourish like grain;[^6] they will blossom like the vine. His fame will be like the wine of Lebanon.
יָשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בְצִלּ֔וֹ יְחַיּ֥וּ דָגָ֖ן וְיִפְרְח֣וּ כַגָּ֑פֶן זִכְר֖וֹ כְּיֵ֥ין לְבָנֽוֹן׃ ס
Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols?[^7] It is I who answer and watch over him.[^8] I am like a luxuriant cypress; your fruit comes from me.
אֶפְרַ֕יִם מַה־לִּ֥י ע֖וֹד לָֽעֲצַבִּ֑ים אֲנִ֧י עָנִ֣יתִי וַאֲשׁוּרֶ֗נּוּ אֲנִי֙ כִּבְר֣וֹשׁ רַֽעֲנָ֔ן מִמֶּ֖נִּי פֶּרְיְךָ֥ נִמְצָֽא׃
Who is wise? Let him understand these things. Who is discerning? Let him know them. For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but rebels stumble in them.
מִ֤י חָכָם֙ וְיָ֣בֵֽן אֵ֔לֶּה נָב֖וֹן וְיֵֽדָעֵ֑ם כִּֽי־יְשָׁרִ֞ים דַּרְכֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה וְצַדִּקִים֙ יֵ֣לְכוּ בָ֔ם וּפֹשְׁעִ֖ים יִכָּ֥שְׁלוּ בָֽם׃

n.1: This verse is 13:16 in most English Bibles, and verses 2–10 are 14:1–9.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: That is, our words of prayer and praise in place of sacrifices. Literally "and we will pay bulls, our lips". The Septuagint reads "the fruit of our lips" (compare Hebrews 13:15), dividing the same consonants differently.
n.5: Probably the cedars of Lebanon, with their deep roots.
n.7: Or "Ephraim will say, 'What more have I to do with idols?'"
n.8: Hebrew *ashurennu*, "I watch over him", sounds like *Ashur*, "Assyria" (compare 13:7).
